title: QVGen: Pushing the Limit of Quantized Video Generative Models
abstract: Video diffusion models (DMs) have enabled high-quality video synthesis. Yet, their substantial computational and memory demands pose serious challenges to real-world deployment, even on high-end GPUs. As a commonly adopted solution, quantization has proven notable success in reducing cost for image DMs, while its direct application to video DMs remains ineffective.  In this paper, we present *QVGen*, a novel quantization-aware training (QAT) framework tailored for high-performance and inference-efficient video DMs under extremely low-bit quantization (*e.g.*, $4$-bit or below). We begin with a theoretical analysis demonstrating that reducing the gradient norm is essential to facilitate convergence for QAT. To this end, we introduce auxiliary modules ($\Phi$) to mitigate large quantization errors, leading to significantly enhanced convergence. To eliminate the inference overhead of $\Phi$, we propose a *rank-decay* strategy that progressively eliminates $\Phi$. Specifically, we repeatedly employ singular value decomposition (SVD) and a proposed rank-based regularization $\mathbf{\gamma}$ to identify and decay low-contributing components. This strategy retains performance while zeroing out additional inference overhead. Extensive experiments across $4$ state-of-the-art (SOTA) video DMs, with parameter sizes ranging from $1.3\text{B}\sim14\text{B}$, show that QVGen is *the first* to reach full-precision comparable quality under $4$-bit settings. Moreover, it significantly outperforms existing methods. For instance, our $3$-bit CogVideoX-2B achieves improvements of $+25.28$ in Dynamic Degree and $+8.43$ in Scene Consistency on VBench. Code and models are available at https://github.com/ModelTC/QVGen.
problem: Video diffusion models demand substantial computational and memory resources, making deployment difficult even on high-end GPUs, and quantization methods fail to transfer effectively from image DMs.
approach: Introduces QVGen, a quantization-aware training framework with auxiliary modules mitigating quantization errors and rank-decay strategy progressively eliminating inference overhead while retaining performance.
contribution: First to reach full-precision comparable quality under 4-bit settings on state-of-the-art video DMs (1.3B-14B parameters), with 3-bit CogVideoX-2B achieving +25.28 improvement.
